claims.problem: Minimal input dimension for superactivation of one-shot zero-error quantum capacity
claims.known_since: Shirokov and Shulman showed that two channels cannot superactivate if one has a qubit input; the smallest dimension where superactivation occurs was open.
claims.ai: GPT-6 Astra (found the pair of noncommutative graphs)
claims.claim: Construction claimed: superactivation with three-dimensional inputs, and additivity for qubits
claims.summary: The paper proves that the one-shot zero-error quantum capacity is additive for any number of qubit-input channels, and gives two operator systems in \(M_3\) with no two-dimensional code whose tensor product has one, so the minimum input dimension for superactivation is 3. The author states that the pair was found with GPT-6 Astra and then checked in exact algebraic form; we checked the code condition numerically.

claims.problem: Slow mixing of quantum Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie–Weiss model
claims.known_since: Left open by Gamarnik, Kiani and Zlokapa, whose bottleneck theorem for quantum Gibbs samplers relies on spatial locality.
claims.ai: GPT-6 (used to prototype the results and help prove the converse of Proposition 7)
claims.claim: Proof claimed: exponential mixing time for the Chen–Kastoryano–Gilyén sampler
claims.summary: At low temperature and weak transverse field, the paper proves that the Chen–Kastoryano–Gilyén Gibbs sampler for the all-to-all quantum Curie–Weiss model needs time \(\exp(\Omega(N))\) to mix, using a dynamical bottleneck theorem on magnetization shells instead of spatial locality. The author states that GPT-6 was used to prototype the results and to help prove one direction of a proposition, with all outputs verified by the author.

claims.known_since: Asked by the Horodeckis in 1998: can every entangled state with a negative partial transpose be distilled? Problem 4 of Horodecki, Rudnicki and Życzkowski's 2022 list.
claims.ai: Generative AI from OpenAI and Anthropic, with an agent memory system, credited with helping find the state
claims.claim: Proof claimed: an explicit NPT bound entangled Werner state
claims.summary: A single-author preprint shows that the Werner state \((23I-3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448\) on \(\mathbb C^8\otimes\mathbb C^8\) has a negative partial transpose yet stays undistillable for every number of copies: no separable operation yields a Bell fidelity above \((1+\sqrt2)/4\). The proof rests on an explicit 4096-dimensional certificate matrix. Our numerical check of its four conditions passed, but no independent review has been reported. If correct, distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

claims.problem: GHZ states of unbounded local dimension from three-photon sources
claims.known_since: Asked by Krenn and coauthors, and by Krenn on MathOverflow in 2019, after two-photon sources were shown to reach local dimension at most 3.
claims.ai: GPT (the paper states that all proofs were generated by GPT)
claims.claim: Proof claimed: three-photon sources reach unbounded GHZ dimension, with matching-order upper bounds and exact nine-path values
claims.summary: The paper constructs networks of \(r\)-photon sources on \(n\) paths whose postselected state is a GHZ state of local dimension at least \(c_rn^{2(r-2)/7}\), answering the question for \(r\ge3\), and shows \(f_3(9)=13\) and \(g_3(3)=6\). The authors state that all proofs were generated by GPT, and their public Lean 4 repository lists the main theorem and the principal supporting results as checked; we did not build the project, but brute-force checks of the nine-path constructions agree.

claims.problem: Attainability of the Rains bound and the depolarizing channel's two-way capacity
claims.known_since: Whether the Rains and relative-entropy bounds give the distillable entanglement and two-way capacities of Pauli channels has been open since Rains (1999) and Pirandola et al. (2017).
claims.ai: GPT-6 Astra (candidate derivations and proofs), with Claude Opus 5.5 for checking
claims.claim: Proof claimed: the bound is attained exactly when a Bell probability vanishes
claims.summary: The authors prove that PPT-preserving distillation of a Bell-diagonal qubit state attains its Rains bound \(1-h_2(F)\) if and only if one Bell probability is zero, and that every mixed entangled isotropic state falls strictly below its bound. So the qubit depolarizing channel's two-way quantum capacity is strictly below the PLOB bound. They state that GPT-6 Astra generated candidate derivations and proofs, which they checked and revised.

claims.known_since: Open since Strassen showed in 1969 that the exponent is below 3; many expected it to be 2.
claims.claim: Exact value claimed: \(\omega=9/4\) over every field
claims.summary: OpenAI's 2 October preprint proved \(\omega\le 9/4\) over the complex numbers; four independent groups have since reproved or extended it, including over every field. The 111-page preprint of 24 November claims the matching lower bound: every formal arithmetic circuit for the \(n\times n\) product needs at least \(n^{9/4}/2\) multiplications or divisions. Its Lean proof covers division-free circuits only, and the lower bound has had no independent review.

sources.label: Amanov, van den Berg and Zuiddam

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Leslie Valiant in 1979; the algebraic analogue of P versus NP.
claims.ai: An internal research Claude model, credited as sole author
claims.claim: Proof claimed: superpolynomial circuit lower bounds for the permanent and Hamiltonian cycle polynomial over every field
claims.summary: A 70-page paper credited to Claude claims that circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, and for the permanent outside characteristic 2, need more than \(m^{c(\log m)^{1/3}}\) gates, also for approximating circuits, so \(\mathsf{VP}\ne\mathsf{VNP}\) over every field. Every numbered statement but one remark is formalized in Lean; the repository checks it with Lean's kernel and the independent nanoda kernel, and a community fork adds two more kernels. Anthropic says no human mathematician has checked the proof, and no machine checks that the statement file says what is claimed.

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Leslie Valiant in 1979; the algebraic analogue of P versus NP.
claims.claim: Proof claimed, with separations of Valiant's whole hierarchy
claims.summary: A 30-page preprint of 23 November claims a border-circuit lower bound of \(\exp(\Omega((\log n)^{5/4}))\) for an explicit VNP family. Two preprints of 24 November supersede it: a grid state sum separates VP from VNP, paths and trees separate formulas, branching programs and circuits, and Hamiltonian cycle and the permanent need \(\exp(c(\log N)^2/(\log\log N)^2)\) gates. The Lean development proves the exact separations; the quantitative bounds are not formalized. No independent review has been reported.

sources.label: VP and VNP are different (23 Nov)

claims.known_since: Open since Watrous (2003): can quantum interactive proofs be compressed from three messages to two?
claims.ai: Large language model tools (OpenAI models through ChatGPT for Academic Researchers)
claims.claim: Proof claimed
claims.summary: A single-author preprint claims \(\mathsf{QIP}(2)=\mathsf{QIP}=\mathsf{PSPACE}\), with a verifier that sends halves of EPR pairs and checks the reply with classical reversible gates. The AI disclosure says language-model tools were used interactively at all stages, from exploration to writing, and that the author revised the manuscript substantially.

claims.known_since: Posed by Riemann in 1859; a Millennium Prize Problem.
claims.claim: Proof claimed, with an extension to the generalized Riemann hypothesis
claims.summary: Alpöge says he found a proof with Claude over several weeks and released it only as a Lean library of about 17 million lines. On 21 November the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified that the library proves exactly Mathlib's statement of the Riemann hypothesis. Independent checks by Andrew Sutherland (MIT) with several separate kernels passed by 25 November, and confirm that the library also proves the generalized hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; other L-functions were not checked. A shorter Lean proof of about 76,000 lines appeared on 25 November and passes the same checks. No human-readable proof has been released. Mathematicians quoted in the press say understanding it will take a long time, and the Association for Human Mathematics objects that no person can take responsibility for it. A separate, human-written proposed proof of the generalized hypothesis by Alessandro Masullo, announced the same day by Ravi Vakil, is in major revision after problems were reported.

sources.label: Lean FRO and Mathlib statement (21 Nov)
Vakil's announcement of Masullo's draft (20 Nov)

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Krenn and coauthors in 2017: linear-optical graphs cannot produce GHZ states beyond the known cases.
claims.claimant: Mario Krenn, Moritz Firsching, George Tsoukalas, Rishikesh Gajjala, Xuemei Gu, Swarat Chaudhuri
claims.claim: Partial proof: impossibility whenever the dimension is at least the number of photons
claims.summary: The paper says the proof was discovered by AlphaProof Nexus and verified in Lean, then explained by the authors. It settles the case \(D\ge N\) of the conjecture; smaller dimensions remain open.

claims.problem: Markov property of high-temperature Gibbs states
claims.known_since: Expected but unproved beyond commuting Hamiltonians and one dimension: decay of conditional mutual information at high temperature.
claims.claimant: Andrew D. Kim, Tai Hsuan Yang, Jong Yeon Lee
claims.ai: GPT-6 Astra (proof found under the authors' guidance), with Claude Opus 5
claims.claim: Proof claimed
claims.summary: The authors prove exponential decay of mutual and conditional mutual information for all local Hamiltonians above a constant temperature. They state that the proof was found with GPT-6 Astra and that they verified and reorganised it.

claims.problem: Super-quadratic advantage of textbook adiabatic optimization
claims.known_since: Open for about two decades, even with black-box objectives.
claims.ai: GPT-6 Luna (main strategy), GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5
claims.claim: Subexponential separation claimed
claims.summary: A black-box objective family is constructed for which the linear-schedule adiabatic algorithm runs in polynomial time while classical algorithms need subexponentially many queries. The paper's AI table says AI devised the approach and developed the proof, but did not pose the question or write the exposition.

claims.problem: Classical simulation of first-order OTOCs in one dimension
claims.known_since: OTOC estimation had been proposed and demonstrated as a route to quantum advantage.
claims.claimant: Laura Lewis, Antonio A. Mele, Ronald de Wolf, Jarrod R. McClean, Amira Abbas
claims.ai: ChatGPT 6 Astra (key sticking points of the proof)
claims.claim: Efficient classical algorithm with proof
claims.summary: The paper gives a classical algorithm with proven error bounds for first-order OTOCs of 1D random circuits at any depth. The authors state that key sticking points were resolved in sessions with ChatGPT 6 Astra after earlier models had failed.

claims.problem: Separating QMA from the QCMA hierarchy
claims.known_since: Includes a question posed by Aaronson, Ingram and Kretschmer.
claims.ai: GPT-6 Astra (initial proof of a weaker separation, proof elements, audit)
claims.claim: Oracle separation claimed
claims.summary: A classical oracle relative to which QMA is not contained in the QCMA hierarchy, by a switching lemma for bounded polynomials. GPT-6 Astra produced an initial proof of a weaker separation and audited the final proof.

claims.problem: Self-correcting quantum memory in three dimensions
claims.known_since: A long-standing question: can a local 3D system store a qubit passively, as a magnet stores a bit?
claims.ai: Gemini 4 Argon ("most of the detailed mathematical reasoning and proof construction")
claims.claim: Partial result: thermal and perturbative stability shown separately
claims.summary: A 3D code family is shown to be self-correcting below a positive temperature and stable under small perturbations at zero temperature, but not under both at once, and with constants far from physical. Standalone existence theorems are verified in Lean.

claims.problem: Vector dihedral coset problem with smooth modulus
claims.known_since: Quasipolynomial algorithms were known only for powers of two; the problem bounds lattice and group-action cryptography.
claims.claim: Quasipolynomial algorithm claimed
claims.summary: A quasipolynomial quantum algorithm for every smooth modulus. The paper states that the main algorithm was found by ChatGPT-5.6 Sol in July 2026 and that the author verified and simplified it.

claims.problem: Simulating the quantum switch with ordered circuits
claims.known_since: Conjectured by Bavaresco and coauthors: no finite number of calls simulates the switch exactly.
claims.ai: GPT, Claude and Gemini models (most technical details and the Lean formalization)
claims.claim: Conjecture proved, with query bounds for approximate simulation
claims.summary: Exact simulation is shown impossible with any finite number of calls, and approximate simulation needs \(\Omega(d^{1/4})\) calls in dimension \(d\). The author states that AI systems worked out most of the technical details and wrote the Lean formalization.

claims.problem: Exact quantum query complexity of composed functions
claims.known_since: Recursive not-all-equal had a gap between Ambainis's exact algorithm and the adversary lower bound.
claims.claimant: Gagan Chiruvella, Chandrima Kayal, Rajat Mittal, Manaswi Paraashar, Nitin Saurabh
claims.ai: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 (main proof ideas)
claims.claim: Composition theorem claimed; closes the recursive not-all-equal gap
claims.summary: Approximate inner evaluations are corrected so that composed exact algorithms cost about the degree of the outer function times a bounded-error inner cost. The authors state that the main proof ideas were generated by GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.

claims.known_since: Posed in 2008; a second claimed proof after Physical Superintelligence's of 6 November.
claims.claimant: Thomas Huffstutler, David Miloschewsky, Supartha Podder
claims.ai: ChatGPT 5 (four months of exploration of the approach)
claims.claim: Short proof claimed
claims.summary: A three-page proof through a completion framework. The authors state that they explored the approach with ChatGPT 5 for four months.

claims.known_since: Posed in 2008; it limits quantum speedups on unstructured problems.
claims.claim: Proof claimed
claims.summary: A 13-page paper and a Lean 4 formalization claim the conjecture. Our background article explains the key lemma and what the Lean development covers.

claims.known_since: Proposed by Impagliazzo and Paturi in 1999.
claims.claim: Refutation claimed
claims.summary: OpenAI says its system found a subexponential algorithm for counting solutions of fixed-width k-SAT. A manuscript and a Lean proof of a slightly weaker bound are public, and an external group is examining the work.

claims.known_since: Half of the Yang–Mills Millennium Prize Problem; the mass gap is not claimed.
claims.claim: Partial resolution claimed
claims.summary: OpenAI says its models proved that four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory exists. The 1,147-page proof has not been released and is with a committee chaired by David Gross.

claims.problem: Local smoothing conjecture, with Kakeya and restriction as consequences
claims.known_since: Central conjectures of harmonic analysis.
claims.claim: Proof claimed in all dimensions
claims.summary: OpenAI claims a proof of local smoothing in all dimensions and derives the Kakeya and Stein restriction conjectures from it. A writeup and Lean artifacts are public; their coverage has not been assessed here.

claims.problem: Haldane gap of the spin-one Heisenberg chain
claims.known_since: Conjectured by Haldane in 1983: integer-spin antiferromagnetic chains have a spectral gap.
claims.claim: Proof claimed for even periodic rings
claims.summary: The manuscript (24 September) proves that the spin-one Heisenberg antiferromagnet on even periodic rings has a spectral gap bounded away from zero, deducing it from finite-ring computations. OpenAI gives no Lean proof, but Sirui Lu has since verified the argument, formalized it in Lean 4 and sharpened the bound to \(\Delta_L>0.0729\) for even \(L\ge36\). Tasaki used its methods to prove uniqueness of the translation-invariant ground state, and Grover extended the argument to higher dimensions.

sources.label: Tasaki: uniqueness of the ground state

claims.problem: Mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
claims.known_since: Zauner conjectured in 1999 that \(\mathbb{C}^6\) has only three mutually unbiased bases, rather than the seven of a complete set.
claims.claim: Proof claimed: exactly three exist
claims.summary: The manuscript (24 September) proves that no four mutually unbiased bases exist in \(\mathbb{C}^6\), by a certified floating-point computation, and a companion proves the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner Fourier-vanishing conjecture outside Tao's matrix. OpenAI's Lean proof covers only the weaker bound of at most five. Cárdenes Wuttig and Tindall have since given an independent topological proof that every triple belongs to a known family and none extends to a fourth basis. Jaswal independently reran OpenAI's computation. Yang, Liu, Li and Deng reproved that no complete set of seven exists without the Fourier-vanishing step.

sources.label: Cárdenes Wuttig and Tindall: independent proof

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Christandl in 2012: composing two PPT channels always gives an entanglement-breaking channel.
claims.claim: Counterexample claimed
claims.summary: A trace-preserving PPT channel on \(21\times21\) matrices whose square is not entanglement breaking, and two PPT maps on \(10\times10\) matrices whose composition is not, from the manuscript of 27 September. Both counterexamples are stated and checked in Lean. No independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Since the Horodeckis and Oppenheim showed in 2005 that some bound-entangled states yield secret key, it has been open whether every entangled state does.
claims.claim: Construction claimed: an entangled state with zero distillable key
claims.summary: The manuscript (27 September) constructs an entangled state on \(\mathbb{C}^{10}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{10}\) from which no secret key can be distilled, for local-instrument protocols with two-way public communication against an eavesdropper holding the purification. The Lean formalization covers the PPT-composition counterexamples from the same paper, not this key statement.

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Guha, Erkmen and Shapiro in 2008; it would settle capacities of several bosonic channels.
claims.claim: Proof claimed
claims.summary: The manuscript (24 September) proves that for a beam splitter of transmissivity \(\eta\) and independent finite-energy inputs in any number of modes, \(N(\rho_C)\ge\eta N(\rho_A)+(1-\eta)N(\rho_B)\), where \(N\) is the entropy photon number. The inequality is formalized in Lean; the paper's capacity consequences are not. No independent review has been reported.

claims.problem: Classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping channel
claims.known_since: Open because additivity of the Holevo information was unknown for this basic qubit noise model; only bounds were known.
claims.claim: Exact capacity claimed
claims.summary: The manuscript (24 September) determines the unassisted classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel as a one-variable optimization, attained by two-state product ensembles. Lean formalizes the additivity over repeated uses and the capacity formula, but not additivity with other channels. No independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Moore conjectured in 1999 that constant-depth quantum circuits with unbounded Toffoli gates cannot compute parity.
claims.claim: Proof claimed in the measured-output model
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September) prove that constant-depth circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed advantage over guessing, when one output qubit is measured. The bounded-error statement is formalized in Lean. No independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Earlier QMA-hardness results for electronic structure, such as Schuch and Verstraete's of 2009, used lattice models, a fixed basis or external fields.
claims.claim: Proof claimed
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September) prove that approximating the ground energy of electrons around clamped unit-charge nuclei, in the full continuum with Coulomb interactions and no basis or external field, is QMA-hard. Both the unit-charge and the binary-charge versions are formalized in Lean. No independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Conjectured by Basso, Farhi, Marwaha, Villalonga and Zhou in 2022: QAOA reaches the Parisi ground-state energy as depth grows.
claims.claim: Proof claimed in the thermodynamic-first limit
claims.summary: The manuscript (25 September) proves that for every accuracy some finite depth and fixed angles bring QAOA's limiting energy per spin within that accuracy of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick ground-state energy, with size taken to infinity first. It gives no bound on the depth. Lean formalizes the Parisi-value identities the argument uses, not the convergence of QAOA itself.

claims.known_since: Shor's algorithm succeeds with high probability; earlier zero-error variants, such as Mosca and Zalka's of 2003, used gates that depend on the input.
claims.claim: Construction claimed: zero-error factoring over one finite gate set
claims.summary: The manuscript (25 September) gives a uniform polynomial-size quantum circuit family over a single fixed finite gate set that outputs the full prime factorization of every \(N\ge2\) with probability exactly one. The statement is formalized in Lean. No independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Exponential parallel repetition for general two-player entangled games has been open; Yuen proved polynomial decay in 2016.
claims.claim: Exponential threshold repetition claimed for every finite game
claims.summary: The manuscript (25 September) proves that if a game's entangled value is \(v<1\), the chance of winning more than a fraction \(v+\delta\) of \(k\) repetitions decays exponentially in \(k\), for all finite-dimensional strategies. Lean formalizes this with a weaker rate in \(\delta\) (\(\delta^{13}\) against the paper's \(\delta^5\)). This threshold form is not the standard parallel repetition question, which asks about winning every round.

claims.known_since: Posed by Aaronson and Kuperberg in 2007: can every unitary be implemented efficiently given a suitable classical oracle?
claims.claim: Positive answer claimed for constant error
claims.summary: The manuscript (5 October) gives, for each \(n\), a polynomial-size quantum circuit with \(H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\) and a Boolean oracle that approximates any \(n\)-qubit unitary to diamond-norm error \(1/2\), for an oracle chosen to suit the target. The oracle need not be efficiently constructible. There is no Lean proof and no independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal proved \(R(f)=O(Q(f)^4)\) for total functions in 2020; a cubic separation was known and a cubic bound was conjectured.
claims.claim: Nearly quartic separation claimed, disproving the cubic conjecture
claims.summary: The manuscript (5 October) constructs total Boolean functions whose randomized query complexity is almost the fourth power of their quantum query complexity, so no bound \(R(f)=O(Q(f)^{\alpha})\) with \(\alpha<4\) holds. There is no Lean proof and no independent review has been reported.

claims.known_since: Hastings proved the area law for gapped one-dimensional ground states in 2007; the two-dimensional case has been a central open problem.
claims.claim: Proof claimed, with efficient PEPS approximations
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September) prove an entanglement area law for unique ground states of gapped finite-range Hamiltonians on square-lattice domains, assuming only the gap of the full system, and that such ground states on \(L\times L\) squares have PEPS approximations with bond dimension polynomial in \(L\). There is no Lean proof and no independent review has been reported.

claims.problem: Spectral gap of the Laughlin state
claims.known_since: A uniform gap above the Laughlin state at filling 1/3 has been expected since the 1980s, but not proved.
claims.claim: Proof claimed, with stability under weak disorder
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September and 5 October) prove a uniform gap above the fermionic Laughlin state for the \(V_1\) interaction at filling \(1/3\) on the sphere, stable under weak one-body potentials. Lean formalizes the uniform gap bound for large particle numbers, but not the stability under disorder. No independent review has been reported.

claims.problem: Spontaneous magnetization of the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
claims.known_since: Dyson, Lieb and Simon proved order for quantum antiferromagnets in 1978; the quantum ferromagnet, and Bloch's 1930 \(T^{3/2}\) law, stayed unproved.
claims.claim: Proof claimed in every dimension from three, with Bloch's law
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September and 5 October) prove spontaneous magnetization of the nearest-neighbour quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in every dimension \(d\ge3\) and every spin, and Bloch's \(T^{3/2}\) law with its exact coefficient in three dimensions. Lean formalizes the magnetization result, not Bloch's law. No independent review has been reported.

claims.problem: Bose–Einstein condensation of an interacting gas
claims.known_since: Condensation of an interacting Bose gas in the thermodynamic limit had not been proved at any positive temperature.
claims.claim: Proof claimed for the dilute hard-sphere gas
claims.summary: The manuscripts (24 September to 5 October) prove condensation for the dilute three-dimensional hard-sphere gas at a positive temperature in the thermodynamic limit, and Bogoliubov's leading quantum-depletion law at zero temperature. Lean formalizes ground-state condensation only, not the positive-temperature result. No independent review has been reported.
